title: Table
summary: Records with the same fields, a row each, read across: the table of the system's prose, in a frame with the large radius that it scrolls in, its head on the surface as an overline, and rows that can be chosen when the task needs it.
use: Records with the same fields, compared or scanned down a column: the registrations of an event, with their names, tickets and fees.
Choosing some of those records for an action, such as the registrations to export: a table whose rows can be chosen.
notFor: Laying out a page: that is the page's grid.
The answers of one record, such as a form's review step: that is a list of terms and values, `ws-pairs`.
A choice of one record to go to: that is a list of links.

parts.root: The frame, an edge with the large radius, in which the table scrolls sideways when it is wider than its place.
parts.th: The name of a column, in the head.
parts.tr: A row of the body: one record.
parts.td: A cell of the body: one field of a record.
parts.amount: An amount in a cell: at the end of its column, in figures of one width, so the digits of the rows line up.
parts.loading-bar: The line under the head while the rows are on their way.

variants.plain: Records to read: no row is chosen.
variants.selectable: Records to choose from: a row is chosen by the checkbox in its first cell, and let go by it again, and a checkbox in the head chooses every row or lets them all go.

sizes.md: Every table: the cells of the prose table, in small body text.

states.rest: Its rows are there, none under the pointer, chosen or with the focus.
states.hover: The pointer is on a row that can be chosen.
states.focus: The keyboard's focus is on the frame of a table that scrolls, or on the checkbox of a row that can be chosen, one at a time. The state table rings the frame of a plain table and a row of one whose rows can be chosen; such a table that scrolls rings its frame as a plain one does while the frame has the focus.
states.loading: Its rows are on their way: the table shows those it has, or none.

keyboard.effect: Moves the focus to the next or the previous checkbox, the head's and then each row's, and to the frame of a table that scrolls. A row is not a stop of its own.
Checks or clears the checkbox with the focus: chooses its row or lets it go, or, in the head, chooses every row or lets them all go.
Scrolls a table that is wider than its frame, while the frame has the focus.

rules: A table of records is a `table` with its column names in `th` cells, so assistive technology reads a cell with the name of its column.
A table that is wider than its frame can take the focus as its frame, so a keyboard can scroll it.

A table whose rows can be chosen is still a `table`, not a `grid`: a checkbox in each row's first cell, named for the row, says to assistive technology whether the row is chosen, not only its color, and a checkbox in the head chooses every row. The rows take no `aria-selected`.
A table whose rows are on their way says so: `aria-busy` on the table while it loads.

forcedColors: The frame's edge, the line under the head and the lines between the rows are real borders, which forced colors keep, so the table keeps its shape when the head's surface and the rows' page color both become the page's color.

A chosen row takes the system's selection colors, `Highlight` under `HighlightText`, kept as they are, so it stands apart from the others: forced colors would paint its fill in the page's color. A row under the pointer has no fill there.
The focus ring of the frame and of a row is an outline, which forced colors keep. The loading line takes the text color, `CanvasText`.
motion: A row's fill changes at once under the pointer and when it is chosen.
The loading line runs along the head only with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. With less motion it stays still, or pulses.
content: Name each column with a noun in sentence case, which the head sets in upper case: Full name, Ticket, Fee.
Write an amount whole, with its currency and the same number of decimals in every row, and put its column's name at the end of its cell, over the amounts: €420.00.
A table with no rows says why in one line in the secondary text color, in place of its rows: No registrations yet.
notes: A table has one size, the prose table's: cells of small body text with 10 px above and below them and 16 px to their sides. The prose table narrows the cells below 64rem, the system's compact width, and a gallery's test runs at a desktop width, so the state table holds the wide one.

The prose table reads the head's colors and the cells' padding from the same tokens, `--ws-table-head-bg`, `--ws-table-head-text`, `--ws-table-cell-padding-inline` and `--ws-table-cell-padding-block`. It draws no rows to choose and no loading line, and lies on whatever is under it.

The edge of the frame and the lines are `color.border`, which is decorative and has no contrast bar: the head's case and the column of each cell carry the shape, and forced colors keep the lines. The line under a chosen row is `color.selection-border`, decorative too: in the light theme the border color is the selection color itself, so it would vanish in the chosen row's fill and run two chosen rows into one, and the line is a step darker there. In the dark theme it is the border color. The last row has no line under it, where the frame's edge closes the table.

A row under the pointer is raised, as everything under the pointer is in the system, and a chosen row takes the selection color, the background of selected text, so the two stand apart in both themes. The text of a row keeps its color on both, at 4.5:1 or more.
The focus ring of a row is drawn inside it while its checkbox has the focus, as a tab's is in the frame: a row fills its frame from edge to edge, which would clip a ring outside it.
An example's rows are its own: the row the helper measures is the first of the body, so a gallery's selected example chooses its first row, and its example at rest chooses none.
